liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Help On The Way** (3 reviews): The Saint Stephen into Help On The Way into Slipknot into Franklin's sequence is called beautiful; Help On The Way is called one of the best, with Phil's opening bass lines pounding authoritatively [15][16][17]
- **Not Fade Away** (2 reviews): Not Fade Away is described as ripping [16][17]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): The first-set Scarlet is called stellar, one of the great Scarlet jams; Lazy Lightning into Supplication also strong [13]
- **Samson And Delilah** (1 review): After a short breather following Samson, the band launches into extended jamming, with Jerry playing focused, bluesy leads [11]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): The latter half of Franklin's Tower is described as ripping [9]

## The recordings

- **gd1976-10-09.aud.falanga.berger.99002.flac24** (recommended): audience recording; 23 songs; 154 min; rated 5/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd1976-10-09.aud.fix-10179.tetzeli.sbeok.83819.flac16**: audience recording; 22 songs; 148 min; rated 3.5/5 by 10 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording was out of phase from an inverted left channel and about 3% fast; both were corrected, leaving it excellent-sounding [3]
- **gd76-10-09.aud.vernon.10179.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 143 min; rated 4.8/5 by 5 [4]
- **gd76-10-09.set2-sbd.miller.12519.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 12 songs; 70 min; rated 4.55/5 by 20 [6]. Said about its sound: The soundboard master is said to do the concert justice [14]
- **gd1976-10-09.set-2.mtx.dan.89544.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 12 songs; 70 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [7]

## Around the show

- Warm late-summer day with sunshine; The Who also on the bill; Jerry played shirtless and slim, which was rare [12]
- Reviewer's college group took a bus to Oakland; the Dead played in the afternoon, The Who afterward, through a huge sound system [14]
- Reviewer recalls Jerry saying in interviews that the band was disappointed with their playing at this show [16]
- Reviewer recalls Jerry saying in interviews that the band was disappointed with their playing at this show [17]
- The uploader says the first set circulates incomplete, and the second set is short but very sweet [7]
- The big sound system felt like the Wall of Sound days, unlike the more refined early-1990s Dead [14]
- Reviewer heard the show was going to be issued on Dick's Picks, prompting a request to restore the upload [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1976-10-09.aud.falanga.berger.99002.flac24**: taped by Louis Falanga; transferred by Rob Berger; source: master taped on a sony tc-152sd [1]
- **gd1976-10-09.aud.fix-10179.tetzeli.sbeok.83819.flac16**: transferred by Pitch correction and other fixes by Bill Tetzeli; source: Unknown aud > ? > DAT [3]. Also: Fixed by re-inverting the left channel and time/pitch stretching tracks in Cool Edit Pro, checked against the circulating soundboard; shntool fixed errors [3]
- **gd76-10-09.aud.vernon.10179.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Marc Pujol; source: Audience Recording [4]. Also: Unknown audience source to DAT, via Dave Minor; transferred by Marc Pujol and seeded to etree by Matt Vernon [4]
- **gd76-10-09.set2-sbd.miller.12519.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [6]
- **gd1976-10-09.set-2.mtx.dan.89544.flac16**: taped by See info file; transferred by Matrixing by Dan Haugh; source: SBD + AUD Matrix Mix (60%-SBD/40%-AUD) [7]. Also: Matrix mix of 60% soundboard and 40% audience, aligned and synced in Cool Edit Pro 2.0, covering set 2 only [7]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Snooky Flowers Grateful Dead: [1976-10-09 Oakland-Alameda County Stadium, Oakland, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1976-10-09-oakland-alameda-county-stadium-oakland-ca-usa/) [22]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Oakland Coliseum Stadium - October 9, 1976](https://www.dead.net/show/october-9-1976) [23]
